problem_statement:
If USB CDC_ACM is selected as a logging backend and the USB cable is not connected to the board at startup, logs are flooded with 'Device not configured or suspended, drop N bytes' warnings. The logging subsystem enables backends immediately after calling their init() callback, without checking whether the backend is actually ready to receive messages.

Backends like USB CDC_ACM require additional time to become operational (e.g., waiting for a USB host connection). The assumption that the backend is always ready after init() returns is incorrect.

The logging backend API needs a mechanism for backends to indicate they are not yet ready. The logging core should defer enabling backends that report they are not ready, and periodically re-check until they become ready.

The failing test creates two backends with 500ms and 1000ms activation delays. Without a fix, both backends are enabled immediately so both receive all log messages. With the fix, backend2 should miss the first log message (it was not yet ready when it was logged), and only receive the second.

Relevant source: include/zephyr/logging/log_backend.h and subsys/logging/log_core.c

See: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/38494

verification.reason: The problem statement describes the general mechanism but omits the exact field name 'is_ready' in struct log_backend_api, the return value convention (0 for ready, -EBUSY for not ready), and the buffering behavior. All are fixable by adding these specifics to the statement without dictating implementation.

problems.detail: The test initializes the new callback as .is_ready in struct log_backend_api, but the problem statement only says 'a mechanism for backends to indicate they are not yet ready' without giving the exact field name is_ready.
The test's is_ready callback returns 0 for ready and -EBUSY for not ready. The problem statement does not specify this return value convention, so the agent cannot know what values to use.

The test relies on the behavior that log messages are buffered (not dropped) until at least one backend becomes ready. The problem statement says 'defer enabling backends' but does not clarify that messages must be retained rather than discarded while backends are not yet ready.

leak_check.leak_detail: The statement names subsys/logging/log_core.c as a file to edit, mentions polling as an implementation hint, and refers to 'the failing test'. These are removable without losing the required public interface or observable behavior. The callback name, signature, return values, header path, and tested behavior are allowed.
leak_check.suggested_statement:
If USB CDC_ACM is selected as a logging backend and the USB cable is not connected to the board at startup, logs are flooded with 'Device not configured or suspended, drop N bytes' warnings. The logging subsystem enables backends immediately after calling their init() callback, without checking whether the backend is actually ready to receive messages.

Backends like USB CDC_ACM require additional time to become operational (e.g., waiting for a USB host connection). The assumption that the backend is always ready after init() returns is incorrect.

The logging backend API (struct log_backend_api) needs a new callback field named is_ready, with signature int (*is_ready)(const struct log_backend *const backend). This callback must return 0 when the backend is ready and -EBUSY when it is not yet ready. Backends that are ready immediately after init() may omit this callback (NULL), in which case the logging core treats them as ready.

The logging core should defer enabling backends whose is_ready callback reports -EBUSY, and periodically re-check until they become ready. Log messages must be buffered (not dropped) until at least one autostarted backend becomes ready; once the first backend is ready, pending messages are processed through it, and subsequent messages go through all ready backends.

For example, with two autostarted backends whose readiness is delayed by 500 ms and 1000 ms (simulated via k_timer), a message emitted before both are ready should be received by the first-ready backend and not by the second; a later message after both are ready should be received by both.

See: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/38494
